item.title: Palestinian officials say Israeli army wounds two in Ramallah raid
item.description:
Israeli army fire wounded two Palestinians on Tuesday during a raid in the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

A hospital in the city received "a young man with a serious gunshot wound to the lower back and a 14-year-old with a live bullet wound to the upper thigh, in addition to numerous cases of suffocation, as a result of the (Israeli army) assault on Ramallah", the ministry said.

item.title: Germany scrambles jets after airline radio glitch sends false hijack alert
item.description:
FRANKFURT, Oct 13 (Reuters) - A flight from Greece to Germany landed safely in Nuremberg on Tuesday after a cockpit hijack alert that the airline attributed to a malfunction prompted the German air force to scramble two fighter jets.

Corendon Airlines blamed a malfunction in the radio communication system and said that "no emergency situation occurred and that at no point were the passengers, flight crew or aircraft in any danger".

item.title: Factbox-MI5 chief lists Iran, Russia, AI and terrorists among threats to UK
item.description:
LONDON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - MI5 spy chief Ken McCallum delivered his annual speech on Tuesday outlining his view of the threats to Britain, from hostile states such as Iran and Russia to the development of artificial intelligence.

Here is a summary of the main threats and issues he detailed in his speech and subsequent questions from media:

item.title: American woman alleged to have joined IS goes on trial
item.description:
An American woman alleged to have been an Islamic State group member caught by anti-IS forces in Syria went on trial in New York on Tuesday, charged with receiving military training from the jihadist group.

Halima Salman, 27, was one of hundreds of women who ended up in the territory controlled by the Islamic State (IS) married to jihadist fighters before being captured and detained pending their repatriation.

item.title: 'Holding our ground': Israel demolishes dozens of Bedouin homes
item.description:
Under an overcast sky in southern Israel, Bedouin villagers wandered through the rubble of what used to be their homes, the latest to be demolished after being deemed illegal structures by Israeli authorities.

The residents of Al-Dahiya in the Negev desert say they have nowhere else to go after bulldozers destroyed around 80 structures housing some 400 people on Monday.

"When night falls, where are we supposed to sleep? Under the open sky, or by the light of the moon -- if there is a moon," said 65-year-old Muhammad Abu Wadi.

item.title: Argentina seeks tribunal order against UK oil activity near Falklands
item.description:
By Aida Pelaez-Fernandez

Oct 13 (Reuters) - Argentina's government said on Tuesday it had filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea seeking to halt British-authorized hydrocarbon activity near the Falkland Islands.

The request aims to prevent theUnited Kingdom from exploiting hydrocarbon resources on the continental shelf of the Northern Falklands Basin, the government added in a statement.

item.title: Iran and Russia are stepping up hybrid campaigns in Britain, UK spy chief says
item.description:
By Michael Holden

LONDON, Oct 13 (Reuters) - Iran is stepping up attempts to hit harder targets such as military sites in Britain and Russia is increasing its hybrid warfare against Ukraine's allies, the UK's domestic spy chief said on Tuesday.

In his annual speech on wide-ranging threats to Britain, MI5 Director General Ken McCallum also said the greatest concern about the misuse of AI was terrorists being able to develop bioweapons or even create new pathogens.

item.title: Egypt's Baha'i minority is running out of space to bury their dead
item.description:
(Refiles to amend reporting credits)

By Yasmine Ghania

CAIRO, Oct 13 (Reuters) - In a Cairo cemetery shaded by palms and tangled shrubs, pale graves are packed so tightly that in some places only narrow strips of sand and broken pavement separate one family’s plot from the next.

This is the last remaining burial place of Egypt's Baha'i community, a religious minority long on the margins of official life, and it is quickly running out of room.

item.title: EU economy chief doubtful Russian diesel exports will affect prices
item.description:
EU economy chief Valdis Dombrovskis told AFP on Tuesday that Russian diesel sales recently authorised by the United States were unlikely to move the price of the commodity, which has spiked since the start of the Iran war.

US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that he had spoken to President Vladimir Putin and they had struck an agreement for Russia to release large amounts of diesel onto world markets, a bid to lower prices that have spiked since the US leader launched the war on Iran on February 28.

item.title: Hezbollah outlines financial aid plan for Lebanese with destroyed homes
item.description:
By Maya Gebeily and Laila Bassam

Oct 13 (Reuters) - Lebanon's Hezbollah will provide up to $14,000 in financial assistance to families whose primary homes have been destroyed or rendered uninhabitable during this year's war with Israel, the chairman of the group's Executive Council said on Tuesday.

Reuters reported last week that Hezbollah had received $200 million from Iran to help displaced Lebanese families, citing two people with direct knowledge of the transfer, though the US disputed Tehran's ability to provide such financial assistance.
